idempotency_key.description: Optional client-supplied key. A request repeated with the same key is never executed again: the service returns the original outcome. Reuse the key when retrying the same request.

args.title: checkout-api health check failures on v2.3.1 — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary:
checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) after the latest deploy of v2.3.1. Observed error rate was 0.18 with healthy=false while all three regions ran v2.3.1.

Action taken: Rolled production back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production (release history: v2.2.9 healthy, v2.3.0 healthy, v2.3.1 unhealthy; v2.3.1-rc is staging-only and was not a rollback candidate).

The first rollback attempt partially failed: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service version reported as "mixed"). A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully across all three regions.

Current state: all production regions on v2.3.0, service healthy=true, error rate down to 0.002.

Follow-up: investigate the orchestrator error that halted the initial rollout, and determine the root cause of the v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy of v2.3.1.

The first rollback attempt partially failed: the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving us-east on v2.3.0 while us-west and eu-west remained on v2.3.1 (service version reported as "mixed"). A retry of the rollback to v2.3.0 completed successfully across all three regions.

trace.final:
Done — checkout-api is recovered and the incident is open.

**What I found**
- All three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) were running **v2.3.1**, reporting `healthy: false` with an error rate of **0.18**.
- Release history: v2.2.9 healthy → v2.3.0 healthy → v2.3.1 unhealthy. (v2.3.1-rc is staging-only, so it wasn't a valid rollback target.)
- Most recent release healthy in production: **v2.3.0**.

**What I did**
1. Rolled back to v2.3.0. The first attempt **partially failed** — the rollout halted after us-east with an orchestrator error, leaving a "mixed" state (us-east on v2.3.0; us-west and eu-west still on the unhealthy v2.3.1). I verified this before proceeding.
2. Retried the rollback to v2.3.0, which completed across all three regions.
3. Verified: all regions on **v2.3.0**, `healthy: true`, error rate down to **0.002**.
2b. Opened SEV2 incident **INC-0001** (on-call paged). The first create request timed out with unknown outcome, so I retried with the same idempotency key; the incident list confirms exactly one incident exists.

**Notes / follow-ups (recorded in the incident)**
- No change-manager approval was required here: v2.3.0 is a version that has previously been healthy in production, so this rollback doesn't meet the policy trigger for approval.
- Worth investigating the orchestrator error that halted the initial rollout, and root-causing the v2.3.1 health check failures before any redeploy of v2.3.1.
